subject: health
unitTitle: Healthy Relationships, Consent, and Digital Boundaries
title: Launch and diagnostic: respect and power
essentialQuestion: How can understanding healthy relationships, consent, and digital boundaries help us explain, decide, create, or solve something that matters?
materials: unit-specific source, model, manipulatives, safe materials, or approved digital tool
keyPoints: Healthy relationships use respect and shared power; control over friends, clothing, location, passwords, money, or communication is a warning sign rather than proof of care.
Use observable facts, reliable information, and the appropriate support route; do not infer a person’s health, motives, or character from one detail.
For respect and power, a strong response distinguishes fact from assumption, uses a fictional or public case, and includes a safe next step or appropriate source of support.
privacySafeScenario: Develop and practice age-appropriate communication, refusal, support, and reporting scripts with no personal disclosure.
studentTask: Apply the lesson facts to a supplied fictional case about respect and power. Produce a three-part response that identifies the key concept, chooses a safe and feasible action, and explains the choice with two details from the instruction plus an appropriate support route.
knowledgeCheck: In two or three sentences, explain the most important distinction in respect and power; use one lesson fact and name the evidence, safety check, or support route that makes the explanation dependable.
completionCriteria: The response completes every named part of the respect and power task using the supplied fictional or public case.
The response uses at least two accurate details from the lesson instruction and distinguishes evidence from assumption.
The response gives a safe, feasible next step or support route and does not depend on private disclosure, body comparison, or recorded media proof.
adaptationChoices: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required. Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model. Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits. Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options. Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media. Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
extensionChallenge: Apply respect and power under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work.

trustedAdultNote: Direct urgent safety or health concerns to a trusted adult or qualified professional.

optionalReflection.prompt: Invite the learner to notice one safe, optional example of respect and power in daily life. No purchase, account creation, photograph, or private disclosure is required.

neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
